extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. It combines diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets plus 3 newly created datasets, and supports fine-grained evaluation with metadata annotations.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was compiled by reusing existing multimodal MathQA and VQA datasets, heuristically filtering VQA examples for math-related content, manually labeling them with expert annotators, and creating three new datasets with manual annotation and review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data included 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA), plus newly sourced puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations such as tables, figures, and charts from online education resources and papers on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 2023 for the PaperQA source papers; no overall collection timeframe stated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For filtering VQA examples, three expert annotators manually labeled whether each example involved mathematical reasoning using a custom annotation tool. Annotators were trained with detailed instructions and examples, and could choose Yes/No/Unsure. Final labels were determined by majority voting. For three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields; each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and disagreements were resolved through discussion to reach consensus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom-developed annotation tool/GUI was used for annotation; Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for the separate human performance study.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was analyzed using Fleiss' Kappa for the mathematical-reasoning labeling task (0.775, substantial agreement). For the newly collected datasets, independent annotation by three reviewers achieved 99.2% inter-annotation consistency, with only 6 disagreements among 736 questions, which were then resolved by discussion.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotations per item for the mathematical-reasoning labeling and the new dataset annotation; five annotators per question in the separate AMT human performance study.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Expert annotators and graduate students in STEM fields; for the AMT study, annotators had completed more than 5,000 HIT tasks and had an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules were used to automatically pre-select likely math-related VQA examples, selecting examples with numeric answers or quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has incomplete coverage of mathematical problems and visual contexts, may not generalize well to other domains, requires labor-intensive collection for high-quality data, has only partial annotations (85.6%), uses heterogeneous non-unified annotation formats, may contain data noise, and the study evaluates only recent prominent models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning in visual contexts could support education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark to evaluate and facilitate development of AI systems for mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, especially LLMs and LMMs, with fine-grained evaluation across tasks such as figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problems, textbook QA, and VQA.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is described as an ongoing research effort; the authors commit to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise based on community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard as new models appear.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using a stratified/random sampling strategy to ensure each source dataset was represented and that testmini matched the overall distribution: first sampling 4 questions per source dataset, then sampling remaining questions proportionally.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Several quality checks were conducted to identify and address errors in the dataset.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: we adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We also conducted several quality checks to address any unidentified errors.
